hypotheses.justification: The statement only uses Nat.card, which needs no finiteness of G. The hypothesis hQcard : Nat.card Q = 512 forces Q to be finite, since the card is nonzero (Nat.finite_of_card_ne_zero). A ≤ Q then makes A finite too. The theorem is therefore true for infinite G. Q is not abelian, because hQZ would give |Q| ≤ 2 otherwise, so z ∈ Q. The argument is the usual pair-counting one, and every step only needs Q and A to be finite. Counting commuting pairs in Q × A works with Fintype Q and Fintype A, which come from Finite Q and Finite A. The step Subgroup.card_dvd_of_le on S ≤ X ≤ Q needs only a finite ambient subgroup. Nat.card_pos on X needs only Finite X. So the helper lemmas (card_comm_dichotomy, two_mul_card_pairs_left/right, card_sq_le_two_mul_of_abelian) can be restated with [Finite Q] in place of [Finite G], or the argument can be run inside the finite group Q. In the current proof, Finite G is used only to produce Fintype ↥Q, Fintype ↥A and Nat.card_pos for these subgroups, and all of these follow from the finiteness of Q. The final nlinarith step does not depend on it. Deleting the argument therefore leaves the statement true and provable.
